fields.message:
Deeply read the information provided by the customer in: {{ enrolled_object.q_a_questions }}

Instruction:
You are classifying the intent of a customer question submitted during a webinar.
Questions may be messy, multi-part, or poorly written.
Your job is to return exactly one category that best describes the strongest intent signal.

🎯 CATEGORIES (9 total)
1. Readiness Intent (Sales-Ready)

Customer expresses active purchasing or implementation intent.
Signals include:

Asking how to order

Asking for a sales contact

Requesting a quote

Requesting commercial pricing with intent to buy

Expressing that they plan to implement and need guidance

“We want to purchase…”

“Who do I speak to about ordering?”

2. Pre-Qualification Intent (Evaluation)

Customer is evaluating feasibility, budgeting, or practical fit.
Signals include:

Cost per sample / run

Throughput / run time

Compatibility with sample types

Kit comparisons

Workflow fit questions

“Can this work in our setup?”

Technical-in-context-of-evaluation questions

These come from people who might buy, but are not declaring intent.

3. General Commercial Interest (Price Curiosity)

Customer asks about product pricing without any indication of intent to buy.
Signals include:

“How much does a flow cell cost?”

“What’s the price of a MinION?”

Purely informational price requests

No request for ordering, quoting, or sales contact

4. Strategic Intent (Future Planning)

Customer discusses organisational or long-term planning.
Signals include:

“We’re planning to expand sequencing capacity next year.”

“We’re evaluating long reads for a future workflow.”

“We’re setting up a genomics core.”

Not a lead today, but meaningful for BD or nurturing.

5. Technical Questions (Support)

Purely technical or scientific questions.
Signals include:

Sample prep

Chemistry

Protocol steps

Troubleshooting

“Can we use tissue samples?”

“How many reads do I need?”

These do not indicate buying intent.

6. Content Requests (Slides / On-Demand)

Signals include:

“Will you share the slides?”

“Can I get the recording?”

7. Technical Difficulties (Can't Connect)

Signals include:

“No audio”

“I can’t see the slides”

“Link not working”

8. Pleasantries

Signals include:

“Hi”

“Thanks!”

“Great talk!”

Greetings or gratitude only

9. Spam / Nonsense / Unintelligible

Signals include:

Gibberish

Off-topic

Advertising

Broken or meaningless text

Extremely short with no content (“q wen Q3”)

🧠 PRIORITY RULES (very important)

If multiple types of content appear in a single message, classify using this ranking:

Spam / Nonsense

Readiness Intent (sales-ready)

Pre-Qualification Intent (evaluation)

General Commercial Interest

Strategic Intent

Technical Questions

Content Requests

Technical Difficulties

Pleasantries



Example:
“Can I order reagents? Also, can we reuse flow cells?”
→ Readiness Intent (highest priority)

Example:
“What’s the price of a MinION, and can I get the slides?”
→ General Commercial Interest

📤 OUTPUT FORMAT

Return a JSON object:

{
  "category": "One of the 9 category names exactly as written",
  "response": "Short explanation of why you classified it this way."
}

🧪 EXAMPLES
Input:

“Who do I speak to in order to order flow cells?”

→

{ 
  "category": "Readiness Intent",
  "response": "The customer is asking how to order a product."
}

Input:

“How much does a MinION cost?”

→

{
  "category": "General Commercial Interest",
  "response": "They request price information without asking to buy."
}

Input:

“Can we use the ligation kit for tissue samples? Also what’s the cost per sample?”

→

{
  "category": "Pre-Qualification Intent",
  "response": "They are evaluating feasibility and budgeting, not asking to purchase."
}

Input:

“Will we get the slides afterward?”

→

{
  "category": "Content Requests",
  "response": "Direct request for webinar materials."
}

Input:

“q wen Q3”

→

{
  "category": "Spam / Nonsense",
  "response": "Text is unintelligible and does not express any meaningful intent."
}
